description:
This week on the DoneDeal YouTube channel we're visiting Copenhagen to test drive a new version of a pioneer in the electric car world - the Nissan Leaf.

title: 2016 Nissan Leaf EV owner says cost of battery replacement may not be worth investment
description:
Neil Turner says he considers himself an environmentalist and an advocate for electric vehicles. Back in 2019, the B.C. resident says he purchased a used 2016 Nissan Leaf electric vehicle.

"The cost was $17,000 CDN including tax,” Turner told Consumer Matters.

Turner says his EV was driving well until this past winter during a cold snap. He says the battery range began to drop a kilometre a second, forcing him to take the car to his local Nissan dealership, where he was told the battery needed replacing.

“We went back and asked, can we have a quote for a replacement battery and that’s when I got the shock,” said Turner.

Turner was quoted over $85,846.55 CDN for the replacement battery. The quote did not include labour costs. “I almost fell down,” Turner said.

Consumer Matters reporter Anne Drewa explains what happened next.

title: The 2026 Nissan LEAF at night is Spectacular - Here's why
description:
#NISSAN #LEAF #EV #TESLA  

The Nissan Leaf has regained its status as the ultimate small EV. At night, the platinum trim shines its brilliance.

The all-new 2026 Nissan LEAF offers a sleek and streamlined design, an effortless charging experience, improved battery range1, and even greater value for money. The 2026 Nissan LEAF will reach Nissan dealerships this fall with Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Prices (MSRP) for the S+ grade starting at $29,9902 – the lowest starting MSRP for any new EV currently on sale in the U.S.3

Nissan's commitment to making EV mobility accessible to all is demonstrated by the new LEAF's MSRP being lower than it was 15 years ago, when the 2011 LEAF carried a list price of $32,780.

Additionally, the 2026 SV+ grade has an MSRP of $34,230, undercutting the 2025 LEAF SV PLUS by $1,960 despite offering dramatically more standard features and an increased driving range.

"The LEAF really kicked off the mainstream EV market when it launched 15 years ago, and Nissan's still committed to making electric driving accessible to all," said Vinay Shahani, senior vice president of U.S. Marketing and Sales at Nissan. "We've stuck to our mission of engineering EVs that are affordable but packed with value. That's how we've kept the LEAF's price steady over three generations — all while giving owners more style, more technology, more features and a vastly improved driving range over the original 2011 model."

The all-new LEAF features a longer driving range of up to 303 miles per charge1, and built-in North American Charging Standard (NACS) compatibility with Plug & Charge4 provides seamless access to more than 20,000 Tesla Superchargers for convenient public charging5, making LEAF ideal for commuting and road trips alike.

LEAF's modern design includes clean, minimalist surfacing and details like motorized flush door handles, a Nissan-first for a production car; a sleek, curving roofline, featuring a katana blade element inspired by the Z sports car; and a segment-first dimming panoramic roof6, which can transition between opaque and transparent at the touch of a button. The airy, spacious cabin features dual displays (12.3 inches, S/S+; 14.3 inches, SV+/PLATINUM+); an open, flat floor beneath the dashboard; and redesigned seats that enhance second-row knee room.

Advanced technology throughout makes living with LEAF effortless and enjoyable. Available Google built-in7, including Google Maps, streamlines navigation with Intelligent Route Planner, and the use of other familiar apps. New-to-LEAF camera tech includes standard, class-exclusive Intelligent Around View® Monitor8, standard Invisible Hood View8 and standard Front Wide View8 functions.

Nissan was among the first mainstream automakers to deliver a truly viable electric car with the launch of the Leaf in 2011. For much of the following decade, it stood as the world’s best-selling EV, only losing that title after the arrival of the Tesla Model 3. Despite that early lead, Nissan has been slow to expand its electric lineup in the U.S., with the now-discontinued Ariya serving as its only other recent EV offering. The Leaf, however, has continued to evolve, and for 2026 it enters its third generation with a full redesign. That timing matters, especially as average new-vehicle transaction prices approach $50,000, and EVs climb closer to $60,000. With a starting price at nearly half that figure, the 2026 Leaf undercuts much of the market and even costs less than the original 2011 model, positioning it as one of the most affordable new electric vehicles available today.

title: Here's my RANGE and efficiency results on the 2026 Nissan LEAF. Skip Tesla?
description:
#nissanleaf #ev #tesla #rangetest 

I test the new 2026 Nissan Leaf's city and highway range. Here's the pros and the cons.

The all-new 2026 Nissan LEAF offers a sleek and streamlined design, an effortless charging experience, improved battery range1, and even greater value for money. The 2026 Nissan LEAF will reach Nissan dealerships this fall with Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Prices (MSRP) for the S+ grade starting at $29,9902 – the lowest starting MSRP for any new EV currently on sale in the U.S.3

Nissan's commitment to making EV mobility accessible to all is demonstrated by the new LEAF's MSRP being lower than it was 15 years ago, when the 2011 LEAF carried a list price of $32,780.

Additionally, the 2026 SV+ grade has an MSRP of $34,230, undercutting the 2025 LEAF SV PLUS by $1,960 despite offering dramatically more standard features and an increased driving range.

"The LEAF really kicked off the mainstream EV market when it launched 15 years ago, and Nissan's still committed to making electric driving accessible to all," said Vinay Shahani, senior vice president of U.S. Marketing and Sales at Nissan. "We've stuck to our mission of engineering EVs that are affordable but packed with value. That's how we've kept the LEAF's price steady over three generations — all while giving owners more style, more technology, more features and a vastly improved driving range over the original 2011 model."

The all-new LEAF features a longer driving range of up to 303 miles per charge1, and built-in North American Charging Standard (NACS) compatibility with Plug & Charge4 provides seamless access to more than 20,000 Tesla Superchargers for convenient public charging5, making LEAF ideal for commuting and road trips alike.

LEAF's modern design includes clean, minimalist surfacing and details like motorized flush door handles, a Nissan-first for a production car; a sleek, curving roofline, featuring a katana blade element inspired by the Z sports car; and a segment-first dimming panoramic roof6, which can transition between opaque and transparent at the touch of a button. The airy, spacious cabin features dual displays (12.3 inches, S/S+; 14.3 inches, SV+/PLATINUM+); an open, flat floor beneath the dashboard; and redesigned seats that enhance second-row knee room.

Advanced technology throughout makes living with LEAF effortless and enjoyable. Available Google built-in7, including Google Maps, streamlines navigation with Intelligent Route Planner, and the use of other familiar apps. New-to-LEAF camera tech includes standard, class-exclusive Intelligent Around View® Monitor8, standard Invisible Hood View8 and standard Front Wide View8 functions.

title: Nissan Leaf 2026 Essai pour @AutomobilePropre @Nissan
Driving the $30K 2026 Nissan Leaf – Is This EV Enough for Nissan’s Comeback?
description:
Back in 2010, when the Leaf debuted, electric cars were still seen as lame, tree-hugging experiments, and the Leaf didn’t do much to dispel the notion. It was slow, offered only around 100 miles of range and suffered from massive battery degradation because Nissan didn’t fit it with a battery cooling system. A fine enough city car, perhaps, but nothing to really move the needle. In the 15 years since, the EV industry has taken great strides forward.

But Nissan hasn’t. At least, not until now.

After a long wait, the third-generation 2026 Nissan Leaf is here. It now offers over 300 miles of range, a seriously improved cabin experience and a new SUV-adjacent design. Most importantly, it still starts at just $29,990. 

Affordable EVs have never been more important. With the tax credit going away, Americans who could pick up a Chevrolet Equinox EV for $28,000 last year will now have to pay $35,000 for the same car. For some people, that’ll be the difference between affording a new EV and having to settle for gas.

But right as the tax credit disappears, Nissan is launching an EV with over 300 miles of range for just $31,485 with destination fees. For a company that has consistently launched middling products to little fanfare, this may finally be the right car at the right time.

Of course, like everyone else, Nissan is also trying to push its cars more upmarket. So while the S+ model is the value king, Nissan only provided the Platinum+ trim to test.

The motor makes 214 horsepower and 262 pound-feet of torque, plenty for a 4,200-lb vehicle with instant torque. And because the Leaf has a 0.26 coefficient of drag and a tidier curb weight than most, it squeezes up to 303 miles out of a 75-kilowatt-hour battery.

Note, however, that the 19-inch wheels and extra weight of the Platinum come with a big range hit. Top-trim Leafs offer just 259 miles of range. And despite the crossover branding, you can’t get one with all-wheel drive. 

Still, with native Tesla Supercharger support and 150-kilowatt charging speeds you can get from 10-80% in 35 minutes. Not brilliant, but in the meaty part of the bell curve for EVs at this price point, and far ahead of cars like the last-gen Bolt and the current-generation Equinox EV.

title: 2026 Nissan LEAF First Drive Review
description:
Fifteen years after it kickstarted the affordable EV movement, the Nissan Leaf is back — smarter, smoother, and more refined than ever. In this first drive review, Matt takes the all-new 2026 Nissan Leaf through Prince Edward County’s scenic roads to find out if the pioneer of mainstream electrification still deserves its reputation as the “Prius of EVs.”

The third-generation Leaf trades its familiar hatchback shape for a sleeker, more 4-door-coupe-like crossover design — but don’t worry, it hasn’t forgotten what made it great. It’s still practical, efficient, and priced for real people, not just early adopters.

Powered by a 214-hp electric motor and a 75-kWh liquid-cooled battery, the new Leaf delivers up to 488 km of range on a single charge, with 150 kW DC fast charging that goes from 10 to 80% in about 35 minutes. The ride is impressively quiet and composed, thanks to a reworked chassis and multi-link rear suspension. Inside, drivers are greeted by available twin 14.3-inch displays, recycled fabric materials, and excellent visibility — a cabin that feels modern yet refreshingly down to earth.

But what really stands out is how *effortless* it all feels. The 2026 Leaf has quietly perfected the art of daily driving. Whether it’s commuting, weekend getaways, or surviving another Canadian winter, this is an EV built for real life.

2026 Nissan Leaf Highlights:
• 214 hp / 261 lb-ft of torque for smooth, quiet acceleration
• Up to 488 km of NRCan range with the 75-kWh battery
• 150 kW DC fast charging (10–80% in ~35 minutes)
• Available Plug & Charge capability via the Nissan Energy Charge Network
• Comfortable, minimalist interior with available twin 14.3-inch displays
• Starts under $45,000 before fees

title: Premier essai Nissan LEAF 2026
description:
Quinze ans après avoir lancé le mouvement des véhicules électriques abordables, la Nissan Leaf est de retour — plus intelligente, plus fluide et plus raffinée que jamais. Dans cet essai routier, Matt met à l’épreuve la toute nouvelle Nissan Leaf 2026 sur les routes pittoresques du comté de Prince Edward afin de déterminer si la pionnière de l’électrification grand public mérite toujours sa réputation de « Prius des véhicules électriques ».

La troisième génération de la Leaf troque sa silhouette familière de hayon pour un design de multisegment plus élancé, rappelant un coupé à quatre portes — mais pas d’inquiétude, elle n’a rien perdu de ce qui faisait sa force. Elle demeure pratique, efficace et offerte à un prix accessible pour de vraies personnes, pas seulement pour les premiers adeptes de la mobilité électrique.

Propulsée par un moteur électrique de 214 chevaux et une batterie refroidie par liquide de 75 kWh, la nouvelle Leaf offre jusqu’à 488 km d’autonomie sur une seule charge, avec une capacité de recharge rapide en courant continu de 150 kW permettant de passer de 10 à 80 % en environ 35 minutes. La conduite est remarquablement silencieuse et équilibrée, grâce à un châssis retravaillé et à une suspension arrière multibras. À bord, les conducteurs sont accueillis par deux écrans de 14,3 pouces disponibles, des matériaux de tissu recyclé et une excellente visibilité — un habitacle à la fois moderne et agréablement terre à terre.

Mais ce qui impressionne vraiment, c’est à quel point tout semble *sans effort*. La Leaf 2026 a discrètement perfectionné l’art de la conduite quotidienne. Qu’il s’agisse des trajets quotidiens, des escapades de fin de semaine ou de la survie à un autre hiver canadien, cette voiture électrique est conçue pour la vraie vie.

Faits saillants de la Nissan Leaf 2026 :
• 214 ch / 261 lb-pi de couple pour une accélération douce et silencieuse
• Jusqu’à 488 km d’autonomie (données RNCan) avec la batterie de 75 kWh
• Recharge rapide en courant continu de 150 kW (de 10 à 80 % en environ 35 minutes)
• Fonction Plug & Charge offerte via le réseau Nissan Energy Charge
• Intérieur confortable et minimaliste avec double écran de 14,3 pouces disponible
• Prix de départ sous la barre des 45 000 $, avant frais

title: 2026 Nissan Leaf – review – back on top? | What Car?
description:
The Nissan Leaf has always been a pioneer — one of the first mainstream electric vehicles that made EV ownership accessible to the masses. Now, for 2026, Nissan has completely reimagined the Leaf to meet the demands of a new generation of electric mobility. The result? A bold, efficient, and high-tech EV that feels more premium and capable than ever.

Exterior: Futuristic and Aerodynamic

The 2026 Nissan Leaf departs dramatically from its familiar hatchback shape and embraces a sleek, fastback-inspired crossover design. Its smooth, sculpted body lines are not just for show — they enhance aerodynamics for improved range and performance.

At the front, the closed grille integrates seamlessly with the LED headlights, creating a sharp, modern face. The new light signature stretches across the hood line, emphasizing width and sophistication. From the side, flush door handles and a gently sloping roofline deliver a dynamic silhouette, while the floating roof design adds a futuristic touch.

Available 19-inch aero wheels and a palette of two-tone finishes complete the sporty and elegant exterior.

Interior: Minimalist Luxury Meets Smart Technology

Inside, the 2026 Leaf feels like a major step forward. The cabin combines minimalist design with premium materials such as soft-touch vegan leather, recycled textiles, and ambient LED lighting.

A large 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster and a 13-inch infotainment touchscreen dominate the dashboard, powered by the latest NissanConnect system with Google built-in and wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto support.

The center console is now more open and practical, offering additional storage space and a wireless charging pad. Rear passengers benefit from increased legroom, while the flat floor architecture makes the interior feel airy and spacious.

Performance: Stronger, Smarter, and More Efficient

The 2026 Leaf is built on Nissan’s latest EV platform, which also underpins the Ariya. Buyers can choose between two battery options — a 60 kWh pack for standard range and an 87 kWh pack for long-range models.

The long-range version delivers up to 440 miles (≈708 km) on a single charge under the WLTP cycle, making it one of the most efficient EVs in its class. With dual-motor all-wheel drive available, the 2026 Leaf produces up to 320 horsepower and 600 Nm of torque, ensuring quick acceleration and confident handling.

Regenerative braking and Nissan’s signature e-Pedal 2.0 enhance energy recovery and driving ease, while the updated thermal management system ensures consistent performance in all climates.

Charging and Connectivity

The new Leaf supports 350 kW DC fast charging, allowing the battery to go from 10% to 80% in just about 20 minutes. Home charging is easier too, thanks to an upgraded 22 kW AC onboard charger.

Remote access through the NissanConnect app lets users check battery status, schedule charging, and precondition the cabin before driving. Over-the-air software updates ensure the car’s systems stay up to date.

Safety and Driver Assistance

The 2026 Nissan Leaf comes standard with ProPILOT Assist 3.0, offering semi-autonomous highway driving with automated lane changes and adaptive cruise control. A 360° camera system, blind-spot warning, emergency braking with pedestrian detection, and driver attention monitoring all come standard.

Its structural rigidity and advanced driver-assist systems make the new Leaf one of the safest EVs Nissan has ever built.

Pricing and Availability

Expected to launch globally in mid-2026, the new Leaf will start around $39,000 USD for the base model and reach up to $55,000 for the high-performance AWD variant. Nissan aims to position it as a practical yet premium alternative to rivals like the Tesla Model 3, Hyundai Ioniq 6, and Volkswagen ID.7.

Verdict: A Reinvented Legend

The 2026 Nissan Leaf isn’t just an upgrade — it’s a rebirth. With its sophisticated design, long range, cutting-edge tech, and strong performance, it’s ready to compete in a rapidly evolving EV landscape.

The original Leaf made electric driving mainstream. The 2026 model proves that Nissan is ready to make it exciting again.

description:
#nissan #leaf #nissanleaf #ev 

In this video I show you the ins and outs of the new #2026 third gen Nissan Leaf. Is it the affordable EV everyone has been waiting for?

The all-new 2026 Nissan LEAF offers a sleek and streamlined design, an effortless charging experience, improved battery range1, and even greater value for money. The 2026 Nissan LEAF will reach Nissan dealerships this fall with Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Prices (MSRP) for the S+ grade starting at $29,9902 – the lowest starting MSRP for any new EV currently on sale in the U.S.3

Nissan's commitment to making EV mobility accessible to all is demonstrated by the new LEAF's MSRP being lower than it was 15 years ago, when the 2011 LEAF carried a list price of $32,780.

Additionally, the 2026 SV+ grade has an MSRP of $34,230, undercutting the 2025 LEAF SV PLUS by $1,960 despite offering dramatically more standard features and an increased driving range.

"The LEAF really kicked off the mainstream EV market when it launched 15 years ago, and Nissan's still committed to making electric driving accessible to all," said Vinay Shahani, senior vice president of U.S. Marketing and Sales at Nissan. "We've stuck to our mission of engineering EVs that are affordable but packed with value. That's how we've kept the LEAF's price steady over three generations — all while giving owners more style, more technology, more features and a vastly improved driving range over the original 2011 model."

The all-new LEAF features a longer driving range of up to 303 miles per charge1, and built-in North American Charging Standard (NACS) compatibility with Plug & Charge4 provides seamless access to more than 20,000 Tesla Superchargers for convenient public charging5, making LEAF ideal for commuting and road trips alike.

LEAF's modern design includes clean, minimalist surfacing and details like motorized flush door handles, a Nissan-first for a production car; a sleek, curving roofline, featuring a katana blade element inspired by the Z sports car; and a segment-first dimming panoramic roof6, which can transition between opaque and transparent at the touch of a button. The airy, spacious cabin features dual displays (12.3 inches, S/S+; 14.3 inches, SV+/PLATINUM+); an open, flat floor beneath the dashboard; and redesigned seats that enhance second-row knee room.

Advanced technology throughout makes living with LEAF effortless and enjoyable. Available Google built-in7, including Google Maps, streamlines navigation with Intelligent Route Planner, and the use of other familiar apps. New-to-LEAF camera tech includes standard, class-exclusive Intelligent Around View® Monitor8, standard Invisible Hood View8 and standard Front Wide View8 functions.

Turn on your Nissan Leaf and make sure the vehicle is in Drive mode.

Press the button to activate the speed limiter function.
Once active, use the + and - buttons to set your desired maximum speed.

The vehicle will not allow you to exceed the set speed limit, but you can still press the accelerator to maintain your desired speed up to the limit.

title: 2026 Nissan Leaf — Japan’s Silent Electric Blade Cutting Through the Future
description:
The 2026 Nissan Leaf does not roar into the future—it glides there, like a neon-lit whisper cutting through the noise of gasoline nostalgia. While others shout with brute force, this Japanese pioneer chooses precision, calm confidence, and an almost poetic restraint. The Leaf has always been a symbol, but in 2026, it becomes a statement.
Visually, the exterior feels sharper, cleaner, and more intentional. The body lines flow like wind-shaped metal, with aerodynamic sculpting that seems carved by electricity itself. Slim LED headlights stare forward with quiet intelligence, while the closed-off grille reminds you this car breathes differently. Subtle blue accents and futuristic wheel designs reinforce its identity as a machine born from Japan’s obsession with efficiency and harmony.
Inside, the Leaf transforms into a digital sanctuary. The dashboard is dominated by a wide, high-resolution display that merges infotainment and driver data into one fluid visual experience. Touch-sensitive controls, minimalist layouts, and eco-conscious materials create an interior that feels both modern and ethical. Nissan’s latest driver-assistance suite works silently in the background, reducing stress and elevating confidence without stealing attention.
Under the skin, the 2026 Nissan Leaf delivers refined electric performance. With improved battery density and smarter energy management, range anxiety fades into irrelevance for daily life. Acceleration from 0–100 km/h in approximately 7.5 seconds isn’t about thrill-seeking—it’s about instant, seamless motion. The torque arrives like a thought becoming action, immediate and smooth.
In the competitive EV landscape, the Leaf stands toe-to-toe with rivals like the Chevrolet Bolt EV, Hyundai Kona Electric, and Volkswagen ID.3. While some competitors chase aggressive styling or raw numbers, the Leaf positions itself as the intelligent all-rounder—balanced, dependable, and accessible.
Pricing remains one of its strongest weapons. The 2026 Nissan Leaf continues to offer exceptional value, undercutting many rivals while delivering proven technology. Long-term ownership is where it truly shines: low maintenance costs, reduced insurance premiums in many markets, and slower depreciation compared to early-generation EVs make it a rational yet emotionally satisfying choice.
On the road, the driving experience is serene and surprisingly engaging. The low center of gravity keeps corners composed, while regenerative braking turns everyday driving into an interactive energy dance. It’s not a sports car—and it doesn’t pretend to be. Its weakness lies in limited high-performance appeal, but its strength is clarity of purpose.
The 2026 Nissan Leaf is not trying to impress everyone. It’s speaking directly to those who understand that the future doesn’t always arrive loudly—it arrives inevitably.
Step into Japan’s electric vision. Drive the silence. Choose the future—now.

title: 2026 Nissan Leaf Review | Specs, Features, Interior, Range and Price
description:
SEO Description

The 2026 brings a new chapter to one of the most recognized electric vehicles in the world. In this video we explore the design, performance, specs, features, interior technology, driving range and expected price of the latest generation Leaf. Built by , the new 2026 model continues the legacy of affordable electric mobility while introducing modern styling, improved battery efficiency and advanced technology for drivers in the United States.

The new Nissan Leaf features a refreshed and more aerodynamic exterior design that looks modern and futuristic. The front of the vehicle includes sleek LED headlights, a smooth electric style grille and sculpted body lines that improve airflow and efficiency. Stylish alloy wheels and a redesigned rear section with modern LED lighting give the car a premium appearance while still maintaining the practical hatchback design that the Leaf is known for. This updated design helps the car stand out among other compact electric vehicles while improving performance and range.

Inside the cabin the 2026 Nissan Leaf offers a comfortable and practical environment designed for everyday drivers. The spacious interior provides seating for passengers with supportive seats and high quality materials that create a modern feel. The dashboard features a digital instrument cluster along with a large infotainment touchscreen that makes it easy to control navigation, music, and vehicle settings. Drivers will appreciate the clean layout and intuitive controls that make driving simple and enjoyable.

Technology is a major highlight of the new Nissan Leaf. The infotainment system supports Apple CarPlay and Android Auto so drivers can connect their smartphones easily. Navigation systems, voice commands, wireless connectivity and multiple USB charging ports make the cabin feel like a connected mobile space. The system also provides useful driving data including battery usage, range estimation and energy efficiency to help drivers manage their electric driving experience.

Performance is another area where the 2026 Nissan Leaf continues to improve. The electric powertrain delivers smooth acceleration with instant torque which makes city driving responsive and enjoyable. Electric vehicles are known for their quiet operation and the Leaf delivers a refined and peaceful ride both in city traffic and on highways. The improved battery technology is expected to provide a longer driving range than previous models making the vehicle more practical for daily commuting and longer trips.

Charging convenience remains one of the key benefits of owning the Nissan Leaf. Drivers can easily charge the vehicle at home using a home charging station or plug into the growing network of public charging stations across the United States. Fast charging capability allows the battery to recharge quickly which makes long distance travel easier and more convenient for electric vehicle owners.

Safety features are also an important part of the 2026 Nissan Leaf. The vehicle is expected to include advanced driver assistance technologies designed to help drivers stay safe and aware on the road. Features such as automatic emergency braking, lane keeping assist, blind spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control and parking assist help create a safer and more confident driving experience. These smart safety systems make the Leaf a strong choice for families and daily commuters.

Another advantage of the Nissan Leaf is practicality. The hatchback design provides flexible cargo space for groceries luggage or everyday items. The rear seats can fold down to create more storage space when needed which makes the car useful for both daily tasks and weekend travel. This balance of comfort efficiency and practicality is one of the reasons the Leaf continues to be popular among electric vehicle buyers.

Overall the 2026 Nissan Leaf represents a smart step forward in the evolution of electric cars. With its modern design improved technology efficient performance and practical interior it remains one of the most accessible electric vehicles for drivers in the United States. The Leaf proves that electric cars can be efficient affordable and enjoyable to drive while still offering the latest automotive innovations.

description:
Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 Review: A Comprehensive Look at the Affordable, Efficient Electric Vehicle

The Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 stands as one of the most popular and accessible electric vehicles (EVs) on the market today. With its environmentally friendly performance, stylish design, and tech-savvy features, the 2020 Nissan Leaf N-Connecta offers an exceptional blend of value, practicality, and sustainability. Whether you're making the switch to electric driving or looking for a reliable EV for city commuting and weekend road trips, the Nissan Leaf N-Connecta delivers a reasonable driving experience. This review will take a deep dive into the specs, features, and performance of the Leaf N-Connecta 2020 to help you determine if it's the right choice for your driving needs.

Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020: Key Specifications

Battery Capacity: 40 kWh Lithium-ion
Motor Power: 110 kW (147 horsepower)
Range: Up to 168 miles on a full charge (WLTP)
Top Speed: 93 mph (150 km/h)
Acceleration (0-62 mph): 7.9 seconds
Charging Time (AC): Approximately 7.5 hours for a full charge (using a 7 kW charger)
Charging Time (DC): 40-60 minutes to charge from 0% to 80% (using a rapid charger)
Drive Type: Front-wheel drive (FWD)
CO2 Emissions: 0 g/km (emission-free)

Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 Driving Performance
When it comes to driving performance, the Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 provides a smooth and quiet ride, which is typical of electric vehicles. Powered by a 40 kWh lithium-ion battery and a 110 kW (147 horsepower) electric motor, the Leaf N-Connecta offers a decent balance of power and efficiency. The car can accelerate from 0 to 62 mph in just 7.9 seconds, which provides a responsive and engaging driving experience, especially in urban and suburban environments.

One standout feature is its e-Pedal system, which allows for one-pedal driving. By simply pressing and releasing the accelerator pedal, you can accelerate, decelerate, and come to a complete stop without using the brake pedal, providing a unique and efficient driving experience.

Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 Range and Charging
One of the key aspects of any electric vehicle is its driving range, and the Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 doesn't disappoint. The vehicle’s 40 kWh battery allows for a range of up to 168 miles on a full charge (WLTP), making it a practical option for daily commuting and even longer trips, especially if you're able to access rapid charging stations along the way.

For charging, the Leaf N-Connecta 2020 supports both AC and DC charging. Using a standard 7 kW home charger, the car can be fully charged in about 7.5 hours, making overnight charging convenient for most users. For faster charging, the Leaf is equipped with DC rapid charging capability, which can charge the battery from 0% to 80% in just 40-60 minutes, depending on the charging station.

Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 Technology and Safety Features
The Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 comes packed with a range of advanced technology and safety features. The NissanConnect infotainment system is intuitive, featuring an easy-to-use interface with 7-inch touchscreen functionality, Bluetooth connectivity, and smartphone integration through Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. The system allows drivers to access music, navigation, and contacts with ease, ensuring that you're always connected while on the road.

In terms of safety, the Leaf N-Connecta offers a suite of driver assistance features that contribute to a safe and enjoyable driving experience. Standard features include automatic emergency braking, lane departure warning, blind-spot monitoring, and rear cross-traffic alert. The car is also equipped with ProPILOT, Nissan's semi-autonomous driving system, which offers adaptive cruise control, steering assistance, and lane centering for a more relaxed drive, especially on highways.

Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 Driving Experience
On the road, the Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 offers a smooth and quiet ride, as you'd expect from an electric vehicle. The absence of engine noise makes for a calm and serene driving environment, and the car's precise steering and responsive acceleration make it enjoyable to drive. Whether you're navigating tight city streets or cruising on the highway, the Leaf N-Connecta feels composed and confident.

Conclusion
The Nissan Leaf offers a reasonably priced car that looks nice and drives way.
The main consideration with the Leaf is it's battery life. Will you be going on long journeys or holidays, sadly not. 
Will it go you to and from work and just about cover the primary function of a car, then yes.

title: 2026 Nissan Leaf Fahrbericht Test Verbrauch Reichweite Ersteindruck | Electric Drive Check
description:
Der neue Nissan Leaf misst 4,35 Meter in der Länge, ohne Außenspiegel 1,81 Meter in der Breite und 1,55 Meter in der Höhe, der Radstand beträgt 2,69 Meter. In den Radhäusern drehen sich wahlweise 195/60 18", 215/55 R18" oder gar 235/45 R19" Räder. Unter der Karosserie, ich zitiere den Held der Steine, nichts vor denen man sich fürchten müsste, ganz im Gegenteil: MacPherson Federbeine vorne, Multilink Hinterachse. Bei der Karosserie selbst: Stromlinienförmige Gestaltung, bündig eingelassene Türgriffe, fließende Dachlinie.

Ihr habt die Qual der Wahl, es stehen zwei Batterieoptionen zur Verfügung: 52 kWh oder 75 kWh. Abhängig von der gewählten Option variiert auch die Peakleistung vom Elektromotor. 130 kW bei 52 kWh oder 160 kW bei 75 kWh. Das maximale Drehmoment liegt mit 345 bzw. 355 Nm fast auf einem Niveau und gleich bleibt stets die Höchstgeschwindigkeit, da wird der Nissan Leaf zugunsten der Reichweite nämlich bei 160 km/h eingebremst.Gleich dürfte auch die 30-Minuten-Dauerleistung sein, die bei diesem Elektromotor bei 70 kW liegen müsste.

Vervollständigen wir das Quartett-Spiel? Die Top-Version beschleunigt binnen 7,6 Sekunden von 0 auf 100 km/h, die Variante mit weniger Leistung benötigt 8,3 Sekunden für den Standard-Sprint und beim Gewicht bringt der neue Nissan Leaf der dritten Generation je nach Modell und Austattungs-Niveau zwischen 1.789 und 1.937 kg auf die Waage.

Was konnte schon der Nissan Leaf Vorgänger? Strom auch abgeben! Auch wenn Nissan aus guten Gründen im Nissan Leaf keinen ChaDeMo Anschluss mehr verwendet in Europa, besteht die Möglichkeit auch wieder Strom abzugeben mit maximal 3,6 kW über einen Vehicle to Load Adapter. 

Ladeleistungen? Bis zu 11 kW an AC, bis zu 105 kW bei der Variante mit 52 kWh und bis zu 150 kW bei der Variante mit dem großen Akku. Nissan verspricht uns, dass man den Ladezustand von 20-80% SoC jeweils in unter einer halben Stunde erhöhen kann, so soll man unter idealen Bedingungen in einer halben Stunde bei der Variante mit großem Akku bis zu 420 km Reichweite nachladen können, denn der WLTP-Wert wird mit 13,8 kWh / 100 km angegeben, die WLTP-Reichweite mit bis zu 622 km beim großen Akku, und bis zu 440 km bei der Variante mit kleinem Akku.  

Bei der ersten Testfahrt von Olli und Steffen hat der Nissan Leaf übrigens 16,4 kWh / 100 km verbraucht, Testdistanz 120 Kilometer, Durchschnittsgeschwindigkeit 48 km/h. Wir erinnern uns? 13,8 kWh/100 km gemäß WLTP, damit hat Olli auf der ersten Testfahrt um ca. 17,4 % überboten hat. Dabei muss man aber auch erwähnen, dass wir bei Dreharbeiten nicht immer besonderes effizient unterwegs sind. Was ich persönlich mag ist das One-Pedal-Driving und die Einstellbarkeit der Regnerationsstufen über die Schaltwippen. 

Das bringt uns nun zum Preis und obwohl Olli die Variante mit dem großen Akku gefahren ist, kann ich euch heute nur den Basispreis nennen von der Variante mit dem kleineren Akku und hier geht es los ab 37.000 Euro und darüber können wir nun fürstlich in der Kommentarspalte diskutieren.

title: 2025 Nissan Leaf Concept: The Silent Storm of Japanese Innovation
description:
The future whispers—and the 2025 Nissan Leaf Concept answers with the grace of a katana slicing through the wind. This isn’t just an electric car; it’s a manifesto of Japanese precision, wrapped in a shell so sleek it seems to defy physics.  

#### Visually Arresting Exterior  
Gone are the meek curves of its predecessors—this Leaf wears a suit of liquid obsidian, its LED blade-lights pulsing like a cyborg’s heartbeat. The floating C-pillar and retractable rear spoiler aren’t just design flourishes; they’re aerodynamic witchcraft, cutting drag to a whisper.  

#### Pioneering Interior Innovations  
Slide inside, and the cabin hums with minimalist futurism. A panoramic OLED dash curves like a samurai’s bow, projecting holographic navigation onto the windshield. The seats, woven from upcycled ocean plastics, cradle you like a zero-gravity throne. And the AI co-pilot? It doesn’t just respond—it anticipates, adjusting climate and playlist before you even sigh.  

#### State-of-the-Art Performance  
Powered by Nissan’s next-gen e-4ORCE dual-motor setup (248 hp, 340 lb-ft), the Leaf Concept sprints from 0–100 km/h in 5.9 seconds—silent, but deadly. The solid-state battery grants 380 miles of range, recharging in 15 minutes flat at ultra-fast stations.  

#### Market Adversaries & Competitive Edge  
The Tesla Model 3 and Hyundai Ioniq 6 loom large, but the Leaf counters with better weight distribution, lower maintenance costs, and a near-silent ride that feels like gliding on magnetic rails.  

#### Pricing & Value Proposition  
Starting at $42,500, it undercuts Tesla while offering superior build quality and Nissan’s legendary reliability. Resale? Strong, thanks to battery longevity guarantees.

This is the all-new BYD Dolphin Surf! 

It’s the second cheapest electric car you can buy in the UK, with the Dacia Spring still holding the crown for the cheapest electric car on sale. The question is, with a starting price of just £18,650, should you choose the BYD over its nearest & dearest rivals? Let’s take a closer look. 

In terms of the exterior design, it’s certainly a bit of an eye-catcher, especially in this luminous yellow paint! There’s quite a bit of black cladding to be found across the car to help break up the colours, although the front end still has an overall strange design. Along the side, you’ll find flush door handles to help with aerodynamics, while at the back, there’s a relatively large boot lid spoiler as well as a full-length light bar - not bad for a car at such a low price point! 

On the inside, the BYD Dolphin Surf comes with a number of qualities you would expect from a car at such a low price point. Bar a couple of areas on the doors and the dash, there are scratchy plastics throughout. Thankfully, the steering wheel is of a good size and comes with several functionality buttons. There is also a digital dial and infotainment screens, but the dials are relatively small and include a very small speedometer, while the infotainment system can be a bit laggy. There are a couple of physical buttons, but there are more rocker-style buttons rather than clickable ones. 

There are two battery options available for the Dolphin Surf - a 30kW with 137 miles of range, or a 43kW with up to 200 miles of range. There are three trim levels and two motor options available: the entry-level 88hp, or a 156hp one.

title: 2025 Nissan Micra EV und neuer Nissan Leaf - 2026 folgt der neue Nissan Juke | AusfahrtTV News
description:
Werbung: Autos sind teuer? Hier findet ihr die akuellsten Leasing-Deals: https://www.rad-ab.com/Leasing-Deals


Mit einem ca. 17 Sekunden langen Teaser läutet Nissan eine neue Ära ein – mit gleich mehreren elektrischen Highlights, die 2025 auf den europäischen Markt rollen sollen. Im Mittelpunkt steht der komplett neue Micra, der als kompakter Stromer mit mutigem Design und einfacher Bedienung an seine erfolgreichen Vorgänger anknüpft. Ihr habt richtig gehört! Der Nissan Micra kommt zurück – als stylischer Elektro-Kleinwagen und die Basis kennen wir auch. Ich persönlich bin heute etwas unscharf, das bitte ich zu entschuldigen.

Der neue Micra wurde im Nissan Design Europe Studio in London entworfen und nutzt die AmpR Small Plattform, die er sich mit dem kommenden R5 von Renault teilt. Zwei Batteriegrößen werden angeboten: 40 kWh und 52 kWh. Damit soll eine Reichweite von über 400 Kilometern möglich sein – je nach Ausführung. 

Gebaut wird der elektrische Micra im sogenannten Ampere ElectriCity-Werk in Frankreich, das eine Schlüsselrolle in der E-Mobilitätsstrategie von Renault-Nissan spielt. Der Marktstart ist noch vor Jahresende geplant und ich kann es ehrlich gesagt kaum erwarten.

Ebenfalls 2025 bringt Nissan eine neue Generation des Leaf – jenes Fahrzeugs, das 2010 als eines der ersten massentauglichen Elektroautos weltweit Furore machte. Die dritte Leaf-Generation basiert auf der CMF-EV-Plattform, die auch beim größeren Ariya zum Einsatz kommt. Optisch soll der neue Leaf mit einer auffälligen, aerodynamischen Formgebung punkten und dann vermutlich auch mit CCS-Ladeanschluss, alles andere würde mich nicht nur überraschen sondern auch schwer enttäuschen.

Die Produktion erfolgt im britischen Sunderland-Werk, das derzeit im Rahmen des Projekts „EV36Zero“ zu einem Vorzeigezentrum für Elektromobilität, erneuerbare Energien und Batteriefertigung umgebaut wird.

Neben den reinen Elektroautos bekommt auch Nissans Hybrid-Technologie ein Update. Die 2022 eingeführte e-POWER-Antriebstechnik, bei der der Verbrennungsmotor ausschließlich als Stromgenerator dient, wird 2025 weiterentwickelt. Verbesserungen bei Effizienz, Emissionen und Fahrkomfort sollen das Fahrerlebnis noch näher an das eines echten Elektroautos heranrücken. Schon jetzt wurden in Europa rund 250.000 Fahrzeuge mit e-POWER-Antrieb verkauft – etwa im Qashqai. Sprich da erwarten wir auch ein Update und ich kann nun schon weiter in die Zukunft schauen, denn der Nissan JUKE - kein Scherz - wird auch elektrisch, denn Nissan arbeitet bereits an der dritten Generation des beliebten JUKE. Der kompakte Crossover soll im Geschäftsjahr 2026 als reines Elektroauto starten. 

Eines muss man Nissan lassen, mit dem Portfolio greift man nicht nach den Sternen, aber durchaus nach wichtigen Marktsegmenten. Ich finde es großartig und sage: Lieber spät als nie, was sagt ihr?

🚗 Nissan Leaf Review (2025)
⚡ Overview:
The Nissan Leaf is one of the world’s most recognizable electric vehicles (EVs), offering a reliable, eco-friendly, and practical solution for daily commuting. Launched in 2010 and continuously updated, the latest Leaf models (especially the 2023–2025 variants) bring improved range, enhanced tech features, and better battery efficiency — all while remaining one of the most affordable EVs on the market.

✅ Pros:
Affordable Pricing: One of the most competitively priced electric vehicles globally.

Eco-Friendly: Zero emissions, quiet operation, and low carbon footprint.

Regenerative Braking: Helps extend battery life and improve efficiency.

e-Pedal Mode: Allows single-pedal driving — intuitive and efficient in urban traffic.

Comfortable Ride: Smooth suspension and quiet cabin.

Good Tech Features: Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, ProPILOT Assist (semi-autonomous driving).

Fast Charging Support: CHAdeMO fast-charging standard.

❌ Cons:
Limited Range (Base Model): The standard 40 kWh battery offers only ~150 miles (240 km).

Older Design Language: Interior and exterior styling is starting to feel a bit dated.

No Liquid Cooling System for Battery: Can reduce battery efficiency in extreme climates.

CHAdeMO Port: Becoming less popular vs. CCS standard in Western markets.

Not Ideal for Long Trips: Due to range and limited high-speed charging network.

title: 2027 Kia EV3 | 320 Miles Of Range With A Tesla Charging Port
description:
The 2027 Kia EV3 made its U.S. debut at the New York International Auto Show, with sales set to begin in late 2026. 

The subcompact electric crossover will get two battery configurations: a 58.3 kilowatt-hour pack with up to 220 miles of range, and an 81.4-kWh long-range pack good for up to 320 miles, according to Kia. The small pack will charge from 10-80% in 29 minutes and the larger pack will do the same in 31 minutes.

We checked the EV3 out at the auto show, and were impressed by its attractive design and great packaging. It looks like a baby EV9, with a boxy design and smooth bodywork.

It comes standard with vehicle-to-load (V2L) bidirectional charging, a NACS charging port for Tesla Supercharger access, two 12.3-inch displays, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto and a panoramic roof. All-wheel drive is available on higher trims, with output ranging from 201 hp to 288 hp in GT guise.

Depending on how Kia prices it, it will compete with the likes of the Toyota bZ, C-HR, Chevy Bolt, and Nissan Leaf among others. Some uncertainties remain around its production location and how Kia plans to navigate U.S. tariffs. But if it arrives at the correct price, it could outsell its bigger siblings and help the automaker regain its mojo in the EV market.

title: Vayve Eva: India’s First Solar-Powered Electric Car Launched at ₹3.25 Lakh | Features & Details
description:
India has taken a significant leap in sustainable transportation with the launch of the Vayve Eva, the nation’s first solar-powered electric car. Unveiled at the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025, the Eva is set to revolutionize urban mobility with its compact design, eco-friendly technology, and affordability.  ￼

Design and Dimensions

The Vayve Eva is reminiscent of small EVs like the Mahindra E2O and Reva, featuring a compact hatchback design ideal for city commutes. It measures 2,950 mm in length and 1,200 mm in width, making it adept at navigating through congested urban areas. Despite its petite size, the Eva comfortably accommodates up to two adults and one child, providing a practical solution for small families or individual travelers.  ￼

Variants and Pricing

Vayve offers the Eva in three variants to cater to diverse customer needs:
 • Nova: Priced at ₹3.25 lakh (ex-showroom), this base model comes with a 9 kWh battery pack, delivering a real-world range of approximately 125 km.  ￼
 • Stella: At ₹3.99 lakh (ex-showroom), the Stella variant is equipped with a 12.6 kWh battery, offering a range of around 175 km.  ￼
 • Vega: The top-tier Vega variant is priced at ₹4.49 lakh (ex-showroom) and features an 18 kWh battery pack, providing an impressive range of up to 250 km on a single charge.  ￼

Solar Integration and Charging

A standout feature of the Eva is its solar roof, capable of providing an additional range of up to 10 km per day, translating to approximately 3,000 km of free driving annually. This solar integration reduces dependency on charging infrastructure, promoting a more sustainable mode of transportation. For conventional charging, the Eva supports DC fast charging, allowing the battery to reach 80% capacity in just 45 minutes.  ￼

Performance and Specifications

The Eva is powered by an electric motor delivering 20.11 bhp, ensuring efficient performance for urban driving. Its compact dimensions and lightweight design contribute to an operational cost of approximately ₹0.5 per km, making it an economical choice for daily commutes.  ￼

Interior and Features

Inside, the Eva is equipped with modern amenities to enhance the driving experience. Features include dual digital displays, a 6-way powered driver seat, and a fixed glass roof, providing a blend of comfort and convenience. The vehicle also offers smart connectivity options, including Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, ensuring drivers stay connected on the go.  ￼

Safety Features

Safety is a priority in the Eva’s design. The vehicle comes with a driver airbag and seatbelts for both passengers, providing essential protection during city drives. Additionally, the monocoque chassis and front crumple zone enhance the vehicle’s safety credentials.  ￼

Conclusion

The Vayve Eva represents a significant advancement in India’s electric vehicle landscape, offering an affordable, eco-friendly, and practical solution for urban transportation. Its combination of solar integration, compact design, and modern features positions it as a compelling choice for environmentally conscious consumers. With pre-launch bookings set to open in January 2025, the Eva is poised to make a substantial impact on the Indian automotive market.

title: Does AC Reduce Electric Car Range? Real EV Test & Tips to Maximize Range in 2025| Electric car facts
description:
In this YouTube Shorts video, we explore a question every electric car owner or buyer has — does using the air conditioner (AC) reduce an EV’s range? The answer is yes, and we’ll show you just how much! Whether you're driving a Tata Nexon EV, MG ZS EV, BYD Atto 3, or any other electric vehicle, AC usage can significantly impact battery consumption, especially in Indian weather conditions.

Electric cars rely on stored battery power for every function — including heating, cooling, lights, infotainment, and more. In hot summers, EV users tend to keep the AC running continuously, which can lead to a drop in real-world range by 10%–20%, depending on outside temperature, battery efficiency, and driving habits.

In this short, we share practical tips to help EV users minimize range loss due to air conditioning. You’ll learn about pre-cooling your EV while plugged in, choosing eco-mode settings, using ventilation instead of full AC, and how speed influences cooling demands.

title: La prima TRAZIONE INTEGRALE (elettrica) di Opel
description:
La Opel completa la gamma della Grandland introducendo la Electric AWD, che affianca le endotermiche, la plug-in e la Electric con motore singolo. Si tratta della prima Opel a batteria con trazione integrale.

Il powertrain bimotore della AWD eroga 325 CV e 509 Nm di coppia, sufficienti a toccare i 100 km/h in 6,1 secondi. Il motore anteriore da 213 CV è lo stesso della Grandland Electric, ma al posteriore si aggiunge una seconda unità da 112 CV; 501 km l’autonomia nel ciclo WLTP.

In questa versione AWD, la Grandland è subito riconoscibile rispetto alle altre motorizzazioni per il design aggiornato dei paraurti e per i cerchi da 20”. Queste soluzioni, insieme ad altri accorgimenti, hanno permesso di rendere questo allestimento il più efficiente della gamma con un Cx di 0,278. La AWD, inoltre, adotta di serie le sospensioni a doppia camera, barre antirollio specifiche e tarature dedicate dell’ESC.

Subaru is officially getting serious about its electric transition with the debut of the 2027 Subaru Getaway. As the first three-row Subaru EV, the Getaway is designed to offer the utility families crave with the rugged, go-anywhere persona Subaru buyers expect. While it shares its foundation with the Toyota Highlander EV, the Getaway distinguishes itself with a more aggressive exterior design, plus it has 8.3 inches of ground clearance and heavy-duty roof rails capable of supporting a rooftop tent.
Inside, this electric Subaru SUV feels more premium than anything else in the current Subaru lineup. The top-tier trims feature Nappa leather, as well as a 14-inch touchscreen interface that far surpasses the tech found in the current Subaru Forester or Outback. Space is a major highlight, too; the long wheelbase provides an impressively roomy third row and a flat load floor for cargo.
Performance-wise, the Getaway aims to be a strong player in the electric 3-row SUV segment. title: My new daily is NOT what you expect
description:

Has Mat finally lost the plot? This week on Carwow, we’ve added one of the rarest cars in the UK to the fleet: the Mia C. It’s a tiny, French electric car built between 2011 and 2013 that is actually rarer than a Ferrari F40! Only 1,000 were ever made before the company went bust.

With only 11 registered on UK roads, Mat sets out to discover if this central-seat micro-car is a misunderstood genius or a total waste of money!

So what exactly is the Mia C? Unlike the Citroën Ami, the Mia C is classified as an actual car, meaning you can drive it on motorways. It features:
- McLaren F1 Layout: A three-seat configuration with the driver positioned in the centre.
- Bizarre Entry: No traditional door handles! You have to press the flower logo to release the electric latch for the sliding doors.
- Performance (or lack thereof): With a choice of 8kWh or 12kWh batteries, it’s "supposed" to have a range of up to 78 miles.

And as you can imagine, it wouldn't be a Carwow video without some punishment. Mat puts the Mia through:
- Real-world Range Test: We drive it until the battery dies to see how close it gets to its 13-year-old promises.
- Performance Testing: Mat records the slowest 0-60 mph time in Carwow history - a staggering 56.49 seconds!
- The Braking Disaster: An emergency stop reveals that the ABS is completely broken, leading to a terrifying 209-foot braking distance! After this, he took a trip straight to the mechanics…

And the trip to the mechanics led to more problems - the struggle to find parts for such a rare car! Mat discovers that many components, such as the rear shock absorbers, were made by companies that build parts for fighter jets and are nearly impossible to source. After failing to use AI to find parts, Mat tracks down specialists in Germany and someone in the UK who actually recognises this specific car from its past life, and helps to get it MOT-ready!

After spending over £1,600 just to get it through an MOT, Mat takes the Mia to Topaz for a complete makeover. The question is, how good will the final edition of the Mia C look? And more importantly, will Mat finally be happy with his purchase? You’ll need to stick around and see for yourself!

title: 2026 BYD Atto 2 Small Electric SUV Review Australia: Price Specs Range
description:
Tom and Joy from the Ludicrous Feed YouTube channel review the BYD Atto 2 in Sydney, Australia, covering the two trims (Dynamic at $31,990 and Premium at $35,990 MSRP, plus ~$4,000 driveaway). The Atto 2 is a front-wheel drive small SUV with a 130 kW motor, 290 Nm torque, 0-100 km/h in 7.9 seconds, a 51.3 kWh BYD Blade LFP battery, and a WLTP range of 345 km. It supports 7 kW AC charging, 82 kW DC fast charging, and V2L. The review walks around the sensible, unassuming exterior, shows the 380L boot with 60/40 split folding seats, flat floor, and no power tailgate. Inside, the Premium trim adds a moon roof with powered sun shade, heated and ventilated front seats, wireless charging, a larger centre screen, 360-degree camera, auto-folding mirrors, and powered front seats. The infotainment runs wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto with physical shortcut buttons. On the road, the ride is described as firm but with some body roll due to height, regen braking is light (no one-pedal driving), and the car feels transition-friendly for drivers moving from petrol or diesel. Charging is tested at a Tesla Supercharger (works via CCS2). The review compares the Atto 2 to rivals like the MG4 EV Urban, GAC Aion UT, Jaecoo J5, Kia EV3, and Leapmotor B10, noting that while rivals may drive better or offer more value, the BYD wins on dealer and service centre availability across regional Australia, strong local support, and an unthreatening, practical ownership experience | Video by Tom Gan (Tesla Tom) and Joy of Ludicrous Feed from Sydney Australia April 2026

title: ₹6 Lakh EV ‘Dead’ Battery Fixed for ₹55K?! The Repair Secret Big Companies Won’t Tell You! #ev #cars
description:
Imagine buying an electric car, enjoying quiet, clean drives, and then one day — your pride and joy refuses to charge. You plug it in, the charger clicks… and nothing. Silence. That’s exactly what happened to the owner of a Tata Tigor EV in a recent case that’s making waves across the EV community.

The car was towed to an authorised Tata service centre. After a quick inspection, the verdict was grim: “Battery pack failure. Needs full replacement.” The cost? A jaw-dropping ₹6,00,000.

For most EV owners, that’s a nightmare scenario. The battery is the single most expensive component in an electric car. If it fails outside warranty, it can feel like the car itself has no future. And in this case, the owner’s battery warranty was already over. No safety net, no manufacturer subsidy — just a six-lakh-rupee bill.

But here’s where the story takes a turn. Instead of handing over that massive sum, the owner decided to get a second opinion — this time from a specialist EV battery repair company called Yanti.

Yanti’s team approached the problem differently. Instead of assuming the entire pack was dead, they removed it from the car and opened it up for detailed diagnostics. Modern EV batteries are made up of multiple modules, each containing dozens of lithium-ion cells. All these cells need to stay in a healthy voltage range and balanced with each other for the pack to work correctly.

What Yanti discovered wasn’t a catastrophic chemical failure, but something more fixable: cell group imbalance. In simple terms, a few groups of cells had dropped to much lower voltage than the rest. The Battery Management System — or BMS — detected this and locked the pack for safety, making it appear “dead” even though most of the cells were fine.

The fix? Patience, precision, and some serious technical know-how. The weak cell groups were brought back to life through controlled, slow charging using programmable chargers. Then came active balancing, where voltage levels across all cells are equalised so the battery can operate normally again. All of this was done under tight temperature monitoring to prevent overheating or damage.

After about a week of careful work, the result was remarkable: the pack’s usable capacity was restored to around 84–94% of its original health. The Tigor EV could charge and drive just like before — and the owner’s wallet was lighter by only ₹55,000, not ₹6 lakh.

This case highlights a big truth in the EV world: not all “dead” batteries are truly dead. Sometimes, the issue is something a manufacturer might not fix — but a skilled independent shop can. Of course, not every battery failure is repairable; severe chemical degradation or physical damage still calls for full replacement. And yes, going outside the authorised network can void any remaining warranty.

But for owners facing out-of-warranty failures, this story is a powerful reminder — before you give up on your EV or your savings, get a proper independent diagnosis. Six lakhs or fifty-five thousand — that’s the difference the right repair can make.

It’s time for another Carwow EV range test!

We’ve got our hands on three of the most powerful EVs that were available at the time of filming - the Tesla Model S Plaid, Lotus Emeya R, and the Audi RS e-tron GT Performance! The question is, which will go further? 

Well, we’re going to put the three to the test as we travel up the M1 motorway. Given these are the performance versions of each car, we’ll be driving them in sports mode, although we may switch to range/eco modes once each car is almost depleted of battery life. 

So, how do they compare? Starting with the Tesla, it’s powered by a 97 kWh battery and three electric motors. These create 1,020 hp, and the car has a claimed range of 364 miles. As new, it costs around £110,000. 

The Lotus Emeya R has dual motors, and these can produce 918hp. It has a 99kWh battery which is good for a claimed range of 301 miles, and as new it cost £131,000. 

Finally we have the Audi. It also has two motors, as well as a 97kWh battery pack. The motors help it produce 925hp, and it has a claimed range of 373 miles. It’s the most expensive car in this line-up, starting at £142,000. 

So which will travel the further - the Audi has the largest claimed range, but could it be beat by the Tesla or Lotus? You’ll have to stick with Mat and the team to see for yourself!

title: Does this new Mercedes change EVERYTHING?
description:

This is the all-new Mercedes CLA! 

The CLA has gone all-electric for the first time, and Mat has flown over to Copenhagen to put this all-new, ultra-modern saloon to the test! 

Let’s take a closer look at the car, starting with the design. Mercedes claims the CLA has a range of an amazing 492 miles, so it’s no surprise that the car is super sleek to help it glide through the air. There are minimal panel gaps across the car, and at the front, there’s a full-length light bar, vents that can open and close to cool the battery, and vents on either side. Along the side, the alloy wheels have been designed to reduce drag, there are smaller side mirrors, and pop-out door handles. At the back, there’s a long boot lid to help reduce drag, and another full-length light bar just like the front. 

The interior of the CLA is super modern! The main statement piece is the full-length screen that stretches across the entire dash! This encompasses the digital dials, the main infotainment screen, and a third screen for the front passenger (the latter being an optional extra). The majority of the cabin is covered in soft-touch materials, and there’s a good amount of storage throughout. The seats are super comfortable, and the infotainment system is super clear and responsive. It also uses the latest version of Mercedes' infotainment system, so it comes with ChatGPT integration. 

The CLA is powered by an 85kWh battery. The car we have here is the CLA 25+, which can produce 272hp and hit 60 mph in 6.7 seconds, while there’s also a more powerful CLA 350 that produces 354hp and hits 60mph in 4.9 seconds. It comes with 320kW DC charging, which gives 200 miles of range with just 10 minutes of charging. That's perfect for the 250+ edition, given that it comes with a claimed range of 492 miles!

The CLA Electric range starts from £45,615, with the range-topping AMG Line costing from £51,770. So is it worth it? Or should you pick up a competitor like the Tesla Model 3 or BMW i4 instead? Stick with Mat to see for yourself!

На выставку XPeng привез и свою новинку этого года гибридный минивэн X9🚗
description:
На выставку XPeng привез и свою новинку этого года гибридный минивэн X9🚗

X9 выпускается с 2023 года и до этого был только электромобилем

Внешне "гибрид" и "электричка" отличаются только по переду: у гибридного X9 немного другие вентиляционные отверстия над бампером🚘

По габаритам: 5.33 м в длину, почти 2 м в ширину и 1.80 м в высоту. Колесная база – 3.16 м🔂

Внутри проекционный экран, 9 подушек безопасности, откидные столики на передних сиденьях, выдвигающийся экран для задних пассажиров, холодильник, электрорегулировка сидений всех трех рядов и т.д😎
Интерьер может быть выполнен в трех цветах

Конечно же много чипов – чип Qualcomm Snapdragon 8295P и три чипа Turing AI (собственные разработки XPeng), они отвечают за работу ассистентов, интеллектуальных 🧠помощников водителю и автономное вождение 2 уровня

Интересно, что в Х9 есть система стабилизации на льду ❄️и снегу: это пневматическая подвеска с большим ходом, интеллектуальная система точного управления с высоким⬆️ крутящим моментом и подруливающая задняя ось

Во внедорожном 🏞режиме автомобиль может развивать максимальный крутящий момент в 4700 Нм

Для сурового зимнего климата 🌨поставили интеллектуальную систему рекуперации тепла. Это увеличивает запас хода в холодном климате

Говорят, что минивэн уже и проверили: в общей сложности за 800 дней испытаний в реальных условиях прошел 20 млн км в 20 государствах и 330 городах

Итого у "гибрида" под капотом 1.5-литровый турбомотор DAM15NTE мощностью 150 л.с. с КПД в 43,06%. И один электродвигатель в 286 л.с.🐎

Батарея емкостью 63.3 кВт/ч дает запас хода до 452 км 🛣на чистом электричестве🔋 и до 1602 км в гибридном режиме🔋⛽️
И это делает XPeng X9 официально самым дальнобойным семиместным минивэном в мире на данный момент 

Расход топлива на 100 км пути в смешанном режиме составляет 6,4 литра⛽️

Пополнить запас батареи на 313 км можно за 10 минут🕑
Кроме того, Х9 может отдавать до 6 кВт электроэнергии сторонним потребителям

Всего на выбор доступно две комплектации по цене 310 и 330 тыс. 💸 (примерно 3,4 -3,6 млн 💸.)

Также XPeng хотят в 2026 году сделать вариант с гибридной🔋⛽️ силовой установкой последовательного типа к чисто электрическому🔋G7 

С середины 2025 года продажи электрического G7 сократился почти втрое, поэтому ребята быстро решили поменять тактику👌

Цены на электрический Xpeng G7 начинаются от 196 тыс. 💸 (2,16 млн.💸)

title: 2026 BYD Denza Z9 GT - 1036km Luxury Electric Shooting Brake
description:
The 2026 BYD Denza Z9 GT has officially launched in China, with five variants priced between 269,800 and 369,800 RMB.

This luxury GT electric sedan showcases BYD’s latest technology, including the e³ (Yi San Fang) intelligent control system, 2nd-generation Blade Battery, God’s Eye 5.0 advanced driver assistance, and DiSus-A intelligent suspension.
The pure electric version offers an impressive CLTC range of up to 1036 km, positioning it among the longest-range EVs in its class.

In terms of design, the Z9 GT continues Denza’s modern family styling. The front features slim split-type headlights and a wide integrated cooling intake, giving the car a sharp and futuristic look.
From the side, the flowing body lines and distinctive “Z-shaped” character line create a dynamic GT silhouette.

The rear design is strong and balanced, highlighted by symmetrical lighting elements and an integrated floating rear spoiler, emphasizing the elegant yet sporty GT character.

Inside, the cabin adopts a striking Lava Red interior theme, inspired by molten lava deep within a volcano. The interior includes carbon fiber trim, diamond-quilted sport seats, a three-spoke sport steering wheel, boost paddles, and a metal column shifter.

Luxury and technology features include:

• Zero-gravity front passenger seat
• Spacious rear seating
• Digital streaming side mirrors
• Smart heating & cooling refrigerator
• Magnetic seat ecosystem
• AR-HUD augmented reality head-up display

The new Z9 GT is available in both pure electric and plug-in hybrid versions.

The PHEV model features a 63.8 kWh battery, delivering 401 km pure electric range and up to 1301 km combined range.
Meanwhile, the EV version offers up to 1036 km CLTC range, making long-distance travel easier than ever.

All models come equipped with the second-generation Blade Battery and ultra-fast charging technology, allowing rapid charging in just minutes.

Introducing the Jaecoo 7!

It’s a mid-size SUV that originated from China, and at the time of writing it is the most configured car on Carwow! With that in mind, Mat’s got his hands on one to see what all the fuss is about. 

The key thing to mention is the price. Whereas competitor cars have seen their prices skyrocket in recent years, the Jaecoo comes in at a respective £30,000, rising to £35,000 for the plug-in hybrid. So when you couple that with a Carwow saving of around £2,500, the Jaecoo easily undercuts its key competitors! 

In terms of the design, it certainly holds a bold presence on the road, and if anything, is reminding us of a Range Rover! Up front, there’s a large, imposing grille which is flanked by headlights that come with graphics built in! Along the side, you’ll find pop-out door handles, and at the back, the car looks smart, with the windscreen wiper hidden at the top of the rear window - just like in a Range Rover! 

There’s a good amount of tech on the inside. All functions are handled through the large infotainment screen, but the system is pretty responsive and intuitive to use. There’s a digital dial screen, a heads up display as standard, and a good amount of storage throughout the cabin. The seats aren’t the most comfortable, but all-in-all it’s a nice place to be. 

There are two engines available: a 1.6-litre 4-cylinder turbo petrol that delivers 147hp and a 1.5-litre 4-cylinder plug-in hybrid that puts down 204hp. The former comes with AWD or FWD, while the PHEV is front-wheel drive only. 

So does the Jaecoo 7 offer enough to sway you away from established competitor brands? Or does Mat think you should stick with what you know? You’ll need to keep watching to see for yourself!

title: New Skoda Elroq Review
description:

Meet the Skoda Elroq! 

It’s an all-new mid-sized electric SUV, and it’s meant to compete with class leaders such as the Kia EV3 and Hyundai Kona Electric. The question is, should the Elroq be at the top of your shopping list if you’re in the market for a car such as this? Let’s take a closer look. 

Regarding the design, the Elroq looks pretty stylish on the outside. Given it’s electric there’s no grille at the front but the split DRLs and headlights help give it presence, as do the grooves on the bonnet. Along the side the satin roof bars stand out to help give it some definition, while around the back it’s all pretty standard, but then again that’s no bad thing! 

Step inside and you might be surprised by how much room there is, especially for passengers in the back! Up front, the majority of the cabin is covered in soft-touch materials, and there’s a large infotainment screen on the dash. Unfortunately, the climate controls are managed through the screen, but at least the system is pretty responsive. There’s loads of storage to be found, and there’s also a digital driver display, although it’s relatively small. 

There are a couple of models available in the Elroq range. It kicks off with the Elroq 50, which is equipped with a single motor for 170hp, a 52kWh battery, and a claimed range of 232 miles. The model we’re reviewing here is the 85, which has a 77kWh battery, a claimed range of 355 miles, and a single motor.

The entry-level Elroq is priced from £31,510, rising up to around £40,000 for the top-of-the-range edition. So is it worth it? You’ll need to stick with Mat to see for yourself!

This is the all-new Renault 5! 

The original Renault 5 was released in the 1970s, but it went out of production way back in 1996. However, it’s now been resurrected in the form of an EV! The question, does the new Renault 5 do justice to the legacy of its predecessors? Let’s take a closer look…

Starting with the exterior design, there’s no denying that Renault has got it bang on! It’s modern yet retro, with several design cues taken from the design of the original Renault 5. Along the side, you get contrasting side mirrors and skirts, and there are different colour roofs available as well! At the back, there are contoured tail lights and fake vents that harp back to the Turbo 2. 

The retro-modern style continues through to the interior. There’s a dual digital dial-infotainment screen on the dash that looks smart and integrated, while there’s a striped design across the rest of the dash to help give it some definition. There may be some hard, scratchy plastics within the cabin, but you have to remember this is still an entry-level car. Thankfully, there’s also a selection of physical buttons on the centre console! The seats not only look retro and cool, but they’re comfortable as well! 

There are two power output choices for the Renault 5. The entry-level is the Urban, which delivers 120hp, 225Nm, and has a claimed 0-60 time of 9 seconds. It also has a claimed range of up to 190 miles. Then we have the Comfort, which delivers 150hp, 245Nm, and a 0-60 time of 7.9 seconds. The claimed range of this edition is 248 miles.

The entry-level Renault 5 starts at £23,000, rising to £29,000 for the range-topping edition. So is it the best small electric car you can buy for under £30,000? You’ll need to stick with Mat and see for yourself!

title: New Tesla Model Y v BYD Sealion: Ultimate review!
description:

It’s time for a showdown between two of the best mid-sized electric SUVs you can buy in 2025 - the Tesla Model Y vs the BYD Sealion! 

The question is, which will come out on top in this all-new group test? Let’s take a closer look at the two contenders. 

The new Model Y has been updated both inside & out compared to the previous model. On the outside, there’s a Cybertruck-inspired front light bar, new alloy wheel designs, and a redesigned rear bumper, coupled with an illuminated Tesla badge. On the inside, it’s still much of the same as in the old car, apart from a few minor tweaks and changes. Thankfully, there’s also still a stalk for the indicator, unlike in the new Model 3! 

In terms of price, the Model Y range starts from £44,990, rising to £52,000 for the top-of-the-range edition. The car we have here is the long-range edition, which has dual motors for AWD, 507hp, 494Nm, and a weight of 1,995kg. 

As for the BYD Sealion, it has a pretty imposing look from the outside, with large air intakes on either side of the front bumper. Around the back, there’s a small boot lip spoiler, as well as a full-length light bar. On the inside, there’s a number of differences to the Tesla. There’s leatherette throughout the cabin that gives it a smart feel, while there are a number of physical buttons and a drive mode select lever. There’s a large infotainment screen that can rotated, and the BYD also comes with a set of digital dials. 

The BYD starts from £47,000, rising to around £59,000 for the range-topping edition. We had the dual motor Excellence edition for this test, which delivers 530hp and 690Nm, and weighs in at 2,420kg. 

The long-term trip computers on these cars recorded energy consumption figures of 3.7 miles per kWh in the Tesla, and 2.5 miles per kWh in the BYD. The Tesla's 75kWh battery means it should manage around 278 miles on a full charge, while the BYD's 91.3kWh battery should deliver around 228 miles. 

So will the BYD come out on top? Or will the Tesla reign supreme? You’ll need to stick with Mat to see for yourself!

description:
BYD เปิดตัวแบตเตอรี่ใหม่ช็อกโลก Blade Battery 2.0 ซึ่งชาร์จเกือบเต็มใน 5 นาที พร้อมกับโครงข่ายชาร์จไวที่มีลุ้นมาไทยด้วย!

อย่าลืมกดปุ่มติดตามและกดกระดิ่ง เพื่อเป็นกำลังใจ และให้ไม่พลาดข่าวสารเรื่องรถ อัปเดตก่อนใครจากพวกเราชาว ‘ที่สุด’ 

สารบัญวิดีโอ:
00:00 Intro
00:52 ข้อมูล แบตเตอรี่ Blade Battery 2.0
04:25 แผนโครงข่าย Flash Charging  + เครื่องชาร์จ 1,500 kW ลุ้นมาไทย!
06:25 ท้าชนสถานีสลับแบตเตอรี่!
07:40 ใช้กับรถรุ่นไหนบ้าง?
08:12 สรุป


สรุป:
แบตเตอรี่ใหม่ Blade Battery 2.0 + โครงข่ายการชาร์จไว Flash Charging 

คุณสมบัติภาพรวม Blade Battery 2.0
- รองรับ DC Fast Charge ชาร์จแบตจาก 10–70% ภายใน 5 นาที และจาก 10–97% ภายใน 9 นาที 
- สามารถชาร์จเร็วภายใต้อุณหภูมิ -30°C จาก 20–97% ในเวลาเพียง 12 นาที
- ต้องใช้กับเครื่องชาร์จรุ่นล่าสุดของ BYD เท่านั้น
- แม้จะใช้เครื่องชาร์จทั่วไป แต่ Blade Battery 2.0 สามารถชาร์จได้เร็วกว่าแบตทั่วไปถึง 30–50%
- ความปลอดภัย : ผ่านทดสอบการชาร์จเร็ว พร้อมกับการเจาะตะปูได้โดยไม่เกิดความร้อนสูงเกินไป (Thermal Runaway) แม้จะผ่านการชาร์จเร็วกว่า 500 รอบ

Blade Battery 2.0 แบ่งได้ทั้งหมด 2 แบบ ได้แก่ Short Blade และ Long Blade

Short Blade 
- เน้นที่การชาร์จไว 
- ขนาดของเซลล์อยู่ที่ 450–580 มม.
- รองรับการชาร์จได้ถึงระดับ 8C และชาร์จเร็วสุดได้ถึงระดับ 16C 
- รองรับ DC Fast Charge จากแบต 10–70% ใน 5 นาที
- ความหนาแน่นพลังงาน 160 Wh/kg
- ไม่ใช่ LFP ทั่วไป แต่จะเป็น Lithium Manganese Iron Phosphate (LMFP) ซึ่งมาพร้อมคาโทดที่ออกแบบมาพิเศษ
- แบตสามารถคายไอออนได้เร็ว และมีค่าการนำไอออนที่สูง ส่งผลให้การจัดการความร้อนดีขึ้น
- มีแผนจะใช้กับรถไฟฟ้าที่มีแบตเตอรี่สถาปัตยกรรมตั้งแต่ 800V – 1000V รวมถึงรถปลั๊กอินไฮบริด (PHEV) 

Long Blade 
- เน้นที่ความหนาแน่นพลังงาน 
- ชาร์จหนึ่งครั้งสามารถวิ่งไกลสุดๆ ยืนพื้นระดับ 1,000 กม.
- ความหนาแน่นพลังงาน 190–210 Wh/kg. เพิ่มขึ้นจากแบตเจนแรก ~40%
- แบบ LMFP เหมือนแบบแรก แต่จะเน้นให้รองรับความหนาแน่นพลังงานที่สูงกว่า 
- รองรับการชาร์จระดับ 3C และสูงสุดถึง 8C 
เหมาะกับรถที่วิ่งไกลๆ

แบตเตอรี่แบบใหม่ทั้งสองยังมาพร้อมโครงสร้างใหม่อย่าง Cell-to-Body 2.0 (CTB 2.0) ซึ่งมีการปรับปรุงจากรุ่นก่อนให้ประสิทธิภาพพื้นที่ห้องโดยสาร 76% รวมถึงทำให้น้ำหนักโครงสร้างเบาลง

โครงข่าย Flash Charging 
- มีแผนขยายไปทั่วโลก รวมถึงบ้านเราด้วย 
- เปิดตัวโครงข่าย Flash Charging ทั่วโลกภายในปี 2026
- ใช้กลยุทธ์ “Flash Charging China” ที่เคยทำในจีนมาเป็นต้นแบบ
- ตัวที่ชาร์จจะมีลักษณะห้อยสายลงมา
- กำลังชาร์จสูงสุดระดับ 1,500 kW 
- สถาปัตยกรรม 1,000V 

โครงข่ายชาร์จไว Flash Charging จะมาไทย เพราะอะไร 
- สร้างความสามารถในการแข่งขันในตลาดหลักต่างประเทศอย่างยุโรปและอาเซียน
- ช่วงปี 2026 นี้ BYD จะขยายกำลังการผลิตต่างประเทศ ฐานการผลิตของ BYD อย่างบ้านเรา จะต้องมีการขยายโครงข่ายการชาร์จ เพื่อสร้าง Ecosystem ให้ครบวงจรสำหรับลูกค้า

เหตุผลที่ BYD ขยายกำลังการผลิตต่างประเทศ
- ยอดขายในต่างประเทศ เพิ่มขึ้น 41.4% (แบบ Year-on-year) ในเดือน ก.พ. 2026

title: New Tesla Model Y: What have they done?
description:

The Tesla Model Y has been updated! 

But this is no ordinary facelift - there are a whole load of changes both inside and out! Mat’s had a chance to get his hands on one before the official unveiling, and he’s about to run you through what’s changed. 

In terms of the design, there have been a whole load of updates. There’s a new bonnet and new wings on either side, and the headlights have been updated as well. A light bar has been added, too, which is giving serious Cybertruck vibes! Along the side, the only changes are new alloy designs, while around the back there’s an updated spoiler, new tail lights that reflect the light across the badge, and a new diffuser. All in all, the looks are a serious improvement over the original Y! 

On the inside the design is almost identical to the new Model 3. However, there’s one BIG change - the indicator stalk has returned in place of buttons on the steering wheel! Elsewhere, the changes are the same as in the Model 3. The seats are comfier and are now ventilated, and the dash design has been updated too. 

When it comes to performance, it comes with the same batteries and motors as the previous car. So this Launch Edition Model Y has dual motors to produce 384hp, as well as a 75kWh battery. There will be a single-motor edition, but the stats are yet to be revealed. 

The previous Model Y had a price tag of £52,000. In contrast, this new edition starts at £61,000 - a £9,000 increase! So is it worth it? You’ll need to stick with Mat to see for yourself!

The time has come for Mat’s mum to change her car! 

A few months ago, she test-drove a couple of different cars with Mat, and her favourite one was the Golf R - and it's finally been delivered!

The thing is, though, it’s fair to say she loved the time she spent with her Tesla Model 3. From the style through to the comfort and performance, she has enjoyed her time in her first EV.

But even though she liked the car, she has still decided to sell it. When asked for the reason, there were a few niggles, from the level of alerts and notifications that the car emits, through to trouble with inflating the tyres, apparently. But there was one key issue that we’re sure many other EV drivers have an issue with - range anxiety. With the limited range of the Tesla, coupled with potential issues when it comes to charging, she has only ever kept herself to short journeys in her Tesla. 

So the question is, once she’s been living with the Golf R for a while, will she prefer it to the Tesla? Or will she be wishing she had kept hold of the EV? And will Mat be able to resell the Tesla for a reasonable amount?! You’ll need to stick with Mat and his mum to see for yourself!
